title: Short-term AI literacy intervention does not reduce over-reliance on incorrect ChatGPT recommendations
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether a brief AI literacy intervention can reduce students’ tendency to over-rely on incorrect ChatGPT recommendations. The authors focus on the behavioral risk of uncritical acceptance of AI outputs, especially when those outputs are wrong, and ask whether explaining ChatGPT’s workings, limitations, and appropriate use can improve decision-making during task solving.

The intervention consisted of a short educational text about ChatGPT, including its statistical working mechanism, prompt-writing guidance, common errors, and limitations such as hallucinations and biased outputs. A control group read only the introductory, general-information portion of the text. After reading their assigned text, participants completed a set of eight Kangaroo math puzzles with ChatGPT recommendations shown alongside each problem; half of the recommendations were intentionally incorrect. Students first had to decide whether to use ChatGPT’s recommendation, making the study a direct counterfactual comparison between intervention and control conditions.

The sample consisted of 36 12th-grade Estonian high school students from 10 schools. The study was conducted online via LimeSurvey in October 2024. Results showed high overall over-reliance: students accepted incorrect ChatGPT advice 52.1% of the time. The intervention did not significantly reduce over-reliance, though it increased self-reported knowledge of ChatGPT’s working mechanism and usage, and it increased under-reliance on correct answers. The authors conclude that brief AI literacy text alone was not sufficient to reduce reliance on incorrect LLM advice, and that decreasing over-reliance may require more than factual instruction about AI limitations.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed experimental study with random assignment, but it is a small single-study RCT (n=36) and only partially addresses the target age range/topic. The design is credible, yet sample size and scope limit confidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The intervention had no significant reduction in over-reliance and showed a negative side effect on under-reliance, so overall impact is unclear to negative. The observed effect on the main target outcome was small and not statistically significant.

interventions.use_case: students used ChatGPT-generated recommendations while solving math puzzles; the intervention tested was a short AI literacy text about ChatGPT's working mechanism, limitations, and wise use before interacting with ChatGPT

finding.finding_summary: This RCT with n=36 high school seniors found that a short AI literacy text did not significantly reduce over-reliance on incorrect ChatGPT recommendations, though the mean over-reliance rate was slightly lower in the intervention group (48.68%, SD=24.26) than in control (55.88%, SD=33.69), Welch's t(28.78)=-0.73, d=-0.25, p=.236. The intervention did significantly increase under-reliance on correct recommendations (36.84%, SD=24.11 vs 19.12%, SD=20.78), t(34)=2.35, d=0.78, p=.025, suggesting a shift toward unnecessary skepticism rather than improved critical evaluation.
finding.measure: Over-reliance and under-reliance rates on ChatGPT recommendations during 8 math puzzle trials; initial decision time on using ChatGPT recommendations
finding.std_deviation: over-reliance SD=24.26 vs 33.69; under-reliance SD=24.11 vs 20.78
